verdict.rationale: Linear's Loops let users describe a job in plain language and set it to run in response to an event. Documented triggers include changes to initiatives, projects and cycles, and a worked example shows a loop updating a launch plan and posting to Slack when a project's target date changes. That directly delivers event-triggered automation for an AI-native user. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of trigger and condition configuration and the full event catalog, plus independent or hands-on corroboration (evidence is changelog-only).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: Loops are a new way for Linear Agent to take on recurring work for your team. Describe the job in plain language and then choose whether it should run on a schedule or in response to an event.
They now respond to more workspace activity, including changes to initiatives, projects, and cycles.
When a project's target date changes, a loop can automatically update the launch plan and post a Slack message explaining what changed, why, and who needs to act.
Automatically turn conversations and customer feedback into actionable issues that are instantly routed, labeled, and prioritized for the right team.
